submitter: bugfix_308_cta_destination_provenance lane — bugs_open/308, the OWNER-COMMISSIONED HAND AUDIT of Phase B and the defect it found
rationale:
Phase B (council 00732119, APPROVED 2026-08-23) widened the CTA label-match candidate set to every page on the site. Its guardian seat objected that this was a wide-surface fleet change with no staged path, and I had listed the same thing as my own top risk: precision was judged by hand on samples, never measured. THE OWNER'S ANSWER WAS TO AUDIT A SAMPLE BEFORE THE ROLL. This submission is the defect that audit found and the fix for it.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND. 50 of the 291 writes were sampled (deterministic, md5-ordered on the row key so the sample is reproducible and uncorrelated with domain) and judged by hand: 34 right, 11 wrong, 5 arguable. NINE OF THE ELEVEN WRONG WERE ONE DEFECT — the button would point at the page it is already on. Census over the full population: **35 of 291 (12%)**. Examples: 'Read the full grip styles guide' on /blog/grip-styles.html resolving to /blog/grip-styles.html; 'Read the policy' on /privacy.html resolving to /privacy.html; 'Read the full terms below' on /terms.html resolving to /terms.html.

WHY THE WIDENING CAUSES IT. A page's own copy is usually the best token match for that page. Before Phase B most pages were not candidates at all, so the case could not arise; the widening manufactures it.

THE PLATFORM ALREADY AGREES A SELF-LINK IS A DEFECT, which is why this is a fix and not a preference: chooseCTATargets' rank() has dropped `h.Name == pageName` since 2026-07-14; applyCTARecompute's keeps refuse a stored value equal to pageURL; and check_misdirected_cta files 'links back to its own page' as a finding. The suggestion side was the one place the rule was missing.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS ITSELF MEASURED, and it is the part I most want reviewed. I implemented the obvious version first — filter the page out of its own candidate list — and measured it: self-links went to 0, but writes fell only 291 -> 281, because 25 of the 35 matched nothing (correct, the button is left alone) while **10 wrote somewhere else, and most of those were wrong**: 'Compare flight shapes' -> the barrel-shapes guide, "Catch up on this week's darts news" -> the dartboard setup guide, 'Talk to FineTuning About Your Automation Audit' -> a blog post about employment law. Once the best candidate is removed, one shared token is enough for noise to win. So the shipped version REFUSES instead: it matches against the full universe and reports no match if the winner is the page itself. Writes 291 -> 256, self-links 0, and nothing diverted to a runner-up.

SIGNATURE CHANGES, DELIBERATE. ctaClassifyAnchor and both writers now take the page's identity. 'Does this copy name a page?' cannot be answered without knowing which page the copy is on, and the compiler is what makes every call site decide — the same enforcement-by-signature reasoning as Phase A's storedCTADestinationIsAuthored. Consumers enumerated: ctaClassifyAnchor has two (check_misdirected_cta, check_cta_nonpage), both in this plan; BestLabelMatchForPage is new.

RESIDUAL, STATED. 13 of the 256 writes land on an About page and 6 of those are wrong — the 'Talk to us about your setup' family, where the only overlapping token is 'about'. Token counting cannot separate them from 'Learn More About Us' -> /about.html, which is CORRECT, and a stopword entry kills both. The owner has ruled this class should be routed to the offer-analyser agent (judgement, not counting); that is a separate piece of work and is NOT in this plan.

plan.summary: A label that names THE PAGE IT SITS ON now names nothing: BestLabelMatchForPage refuses it, both CTA writers and the misdirected-CTA detector pass their page identity, and the refusal is deliberately not a pre-filter. Found by the owner-commissioned hand audit of Phase B's 291 writes; 35 of them (12%) pointed a button at its own page.

edits.rationale: The fix itself. A label naming THE PAGE IT SITS ON names nothing, so ok=false and both writers' keep branches hold the stored value. It REFUSES rather than pre-filtering, and that distinction is the measured part: filtering the page out and letting the runner-up win was implemented first, then measured — 25 of the 35 self-linking rows then matched nothing (correct) but 10 wrote somewhere else and most were wrong ("Compare flight shapes" -> the barrel-shapes guide; "Catch up on this week's darts news" -> the dartboard setup guide). Once the best candidate is removed, one shared token is enough for noise to win. Copy that names its own page is a CONTENT defect, not a destination to guess at.

REAL DIFF, generated from the working tree (uncommitted at submission time):

@@ -118,3 +118,56 @@ func LoadCTALabelUniverse(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, siteID uuid.UUID) ([]
 	}
 	return out, nil
 }
+
+// BestLabelMatchForPage is BestLabelMatch with one extra rule: a label that
+// names THE PAGE IT SITS ON names nothing. It reports ok=false, which for both
+// CTA writers means their keep branches hold the stored value, and for the
+// detector means no finding is filed.
+//
+// WHY THIS EXISTS — measured, not anticipated. The owner asked for the Phase B
+// widening to be hand-audited before it rolled (2026-08-23). **35 of the 291
+// writes it would have performed — 12% — pointed a button at the page it was
+// already on**: "Read the full grip styles guide" on /blog/grip-styles.html
+// resolving to /blog/grip-styles.html; "Read the policy" on /privacy.html
+// resolving to /privacy.html; 33 more. The widening is what manufactures them,
+// because a page's own copy is usually the best token match for that page and
+// before Phase B most pages were not candidates at all.
+//
+// THE PLATFORM ALREADY AGREES A SELF-LINK IS A DEFECT, in three places, which is
+// why this is a fix rather than a preference:
+//   - chooseCTATargets' rank() has dropped `h.Name == pageName` since
+//     2026-07-14 ("don't point a page's hero at itself");
+//   - applyCTARecompute's keeps refuse a stored value equal to pageURL;
+//   - check_misdirected_cta files "links back to its own page" as a finding —
+//     so suggesting one as the REPAIR was the same defect from the other side.
+//
+// ⚠ REFUSING IS NOT THE SAME AS DROPPING THE PAGE FROM THE POOL, and the
+// difference was measured too. Filtering the page out first and letting the
+// runner-up win was tried: **25 of the 35 then matched nothing (correct — the
+// button is left alone), but 10 wrote somewhere else, and most of those were
+// wrong** — "Compare flight shapes" landing on the barrel-shapes guide,
+// "Catch up on this week's darts news" on the dartboard setup guide,
+// "Talk to FineTuning About Your Automation Audit" on a blog post about
+// employment law. Once the best candidate is removed, a single shared token is
+// enough for noise to win. So the answer is NO OPINION, exactly as for an
+// ambiguous tie: copy that names its own page is a CONTENT defect (the button
+// should not be there), not a destination the matcher should guess at.
+//
+// Match on NAME or URL because the two diverge and callers hold different ones:
+// the build path knows `page_name` only, the repair path knows both, and a
+// page's name is frequently not its URL stem (`grip-styles` lives at
+// /blog/grip-styles.html). Pass "" for whichever you lack.
+func BestLabelMatchForPage(label string, candidates []LabelMatchCandidate,
+	pageName, pageURL string) (best LabelMatchCandidate, ok bool, ambiguous bool) {
+	best, ok, ambiguous = BestLabelMatch(label, candidates)
+	if !ok {
+		return best, ok, ambiguous
+	}
+	if pageName != "" && best.Name == pageName {
+		return LabelMatchCandidate{}, false, false
+	}
+	if pageURL != "" && NormalizePagePath(best.URL) == NormalizePagePath(pageURL) {
+		return LabelMatchCandidate{}, false, false
+	}
+	return best, true, false
+}

edits.rationale: BUILD writer. setCTAField takes the page name so the match can refuse the page it is on; this path has no page URL, and pageName is the same key rank() has used for the positional pick since 2026-07-14.

REPAIR writer. rerenderCTAState carries the page's own name and URL; applyCTARecompute takes pageName (it already had pageURL). Both keys are used because a page's name is frequently not its URL stem — dartsonline's grip-styles page lives at /blog/grip-styles.html, which is why a name-only test would have missed it.

DETECTOR. The page identity becomes a parameter because "does this copy name a page?" cannot be answered without knowing which page the copy is ON. This check already files the mirror-image defect ('links back to its own page') against the href, so suggesting a self-link as the REPAIR was the same defect from the other direction. Keeping the detector and the writers on one rule is the whole of bug 308.
The sibling consumer of ctaClassifyAnchor, threaded through unchanged in behaviour. Its caller already had pageName/pageURL in scope.

The pin, and its FIXTURE is load-bearing. The first version used a runner-up sharing no token with the label, so both the refusal and the pre-filter returned 'no match' and the pre-filter mutation PASSED. Rewritten around the real measured case (flight-shapes vs barrel-shapes, which share 'shapes'), plus an assertion that the fixture is not inert: with the page removed, the runner-up must still match. Mutation-proven both ways after that change.

grounded_in: Owner instruction 2026-08-23: audit a sample of the widening's writes before the roll. This submission is what the audit produced.
Hand audit, 50 of 291 writes, deterministic md5-ordered sample: 34 right, 11 wrong, 5 arguable. 9 of the 11 wrong were self-links.
Census over the full population: 35 of 291 writes (12%) resolved to the page the button sits on.

Pre-filter version implemented and MEASURED before being rejected: writes 291 -> 281, self-links 0, but 10 rows diverted to a runner-up and most were wrong. Refusal version: writes 291 -> 256, self-links 0, no diversions.

The platform already treats a self-link as a defect in three places: rank()'s `h.Name == pageName` (since 2026-07-14), applyCTARecompute's keeps vs pageURL, and check_misdirected_cta's 'links back to its own page' arm.
A page's name is frequently not its URL stem — dartsonline's `grip-styles` lives at /blog/grip-styles.html — so the predicate takes both keys and a name-only test would have missed that row.

Mutation-proven against a clean `git archive HEAD` tree: (a) turning the refusal into a pre-filter fails the pin; (b) dropping the URL key fails it. The FIRST fixture could not discriminate (a) — the runner-up shared no token with the label, so both implementations returned 'no match' and the mutation passed. The fixture was rebuilt around the real measured case and now asserts it is not inert.
Full ./platform/orchestration/... suite green on a clean HEAD tree plus this change.
plan.risks:
1. RECALL. A button whose copy genuinely names its own page now resolves to nothing rather than to a second-best page. That is the intent, and 25 of the 35 already behaved that way under the pre-filter — but it means the platform is silent about a real content defect ('Read the policy' on the policy page is a button that should not exist). No finding is filed for it, and this change does not add one.

2. THE DETECTOR GOES QUIETER TOO. ctaClassifyAnchor returning named=false for a self-naming anchor means no misdirected_cta finding. That is the convergence this bug is about — the checker must not suggest what the repairer will refuse — but it is a reduction in reported findings that nobody will see happen.

3. THE ABOUT-PAGE RESIDUAL IS UNFIXED, 6 wrong writes of 256, and is explicitly deferred to the offer-analyser per the owner's ruling. It will ship.

4. PRECISION AFTER THE FIX IS STILL A SAMPLE, not a rate: the audit's 34/11/5 was taken BEFORE this change. The 11 wrong included 9 self-links now fixed, which implies roughly 43 right / 2 wrong / 5 arguable of 50 — but that is arithmetic on the old sample, not a fresh audit, and I am not presenting it as one.
